remaining_gaps.topic: One Presence loss per simultaneous Blight addition, not per Blight token
remaining_gaps.question: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose? Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: The simultaneous addition destroys one Presence from each Spirit, even though two Blight tokens are added. Two separate additions destroy one Presence per Spirit on each addition, hence two per Spirit if available. Cascades elsewhere are outside the requested count.
remaining_gaps.novelty_basis: This is the FAQ's explicit one-or-more-Blight rule and its temporal unit of resolution. Changing simultaneous versus separate instructions changes the Presence-loss outcome; it is not a changed-number example of the ordinary one-Blight rule. The simultaneous-Blight premise is an explicit given, with no excluded producer imported.
remaining_gaps.why_existing_prompts_do_not_cover: Q13 adds a single new Blight. Q44 tests cascade revisits and existing Blight quantity; those are separate additions. Q94 supplies two simultaneous Blight but requests the old-pool carryover, flip effects, and timing of addition, never Presence loss. Q108 tests which Presence may be destroyed. None asks whether multiple tokens in one addition destroy multiple disks.
remaining_gaps.map_issue: The blight-cascade map paraphrase says each addition destroys one Presence, omitting the source's operative one-or-more distinction; Q44/Q46 do not test that branch. The general all-passages-mapped claim cannot credit an unrequested outcome.

remaining_gaps.topic: Concealing Shadows protection is limited to Damage from Ravaging Invaders
remaining_gaps.question: Concealing Shadows has resolved on a land. Later that turn, Poisoned Land resolves there and instructs the Spirit to destroy all Dahan. Does Concealing Shadows prevent those destructions? If Infinite Vitality's threshold had also resolved on that land this turn, would that threshold prevent them?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Concealing Shadows does not prevent them: its protection is only against Damage from Ravaging Invaders, while Poisoned Land explicitly Destroys Dahan. Infinite Vitality's threshold makes those Dahan ignore Damage and Destruction effects, so it prevents that destruction.
remaining_gaps.novelty_basis: A named core protection has a source/type boundary. This directly tests the consequential uncovered branch where Dahan survive the Ravage-only protection yet remain vulnerable to a core Power's Destroy instruction; it is not another Ravage arithmetic example.
remaining_gaps.why_existing_prompts_do_not_cover: Q115 uses only Ravaging Invader Damage and asks the land/Dahan split and counterattack. It never challenges protection from another source or a direct Destroy instruction. Q65 tests Infinite Vitality against Remove/Replace and cascade selection, not the narrower boundary of Concealing Shadows. Q18 distinguishes Damage and Destroy generally, but does not ask which protection reaches a direct Destroy.
remaining_gaps.map_issue: The concealing-dahan-only row itself claims Direct Destroy and other-source Damage are outside its protection while mapping only to Q115. Those are extra source facts beyond Q115's actual requested Ravage outcome and earn no coverage credit.
